# Seniors of NJ

> The home for older adults in New Jersey. Independent, plain-English guides to New Jersey senior benefits (ANCHOR, Senior Freeze, Stay NJ, PAAD, LIHEAP), Medicare, caregiving, housing, things to do and ways to learn, work and meet people. Every guide cites official sources and shows the date it was last updated. Not a government agency.

## Benefits & Money

- [ANCHOR, Senior Freeze and Stay NJ: the complete 2026 guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/property-tax-relief-nj/): One form unlocks all three of New Jersey's property tax relief programs for seniors. Here is who qualifies, how much you could get, and how to file the PAS-1 before November 2.
- [PAAD, Senior Gold and Medicare help: how NJ seniors save](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/prescription-and-bill-help/): One New Jersey application can cut your prescription copays to $5, pay your Medicare premium and add $225 a year for utilities. Here is who qualifies in 2026.
- [Social Security's 3.6% raise for 2027: what it means in NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/social-security-2027/): Checks grow in January, but Medicare, the earnings test and your claiming age all shape what you actually keep. Plus how New Jersey taxes retirement income.
- [Food and utility help for New Jersey seniors: where to start](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/food-and-utility-help/): SNAP, senior meals, farmers market benefits, heating aid and free weatherization can all ease a tight budget. Here is how each works and how to apply this season.
- [Working after 60 in New Jersey: jobs, training and your rights](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/working-after-60-nj/): Part-time work, paid training through SCSEP or a second career can all make sense after 60. Here is where to find help in New Jersey and how a paycheck affects Social Security, Medicare and taxes.

## Health & Medicare

- [Medicare 101 for New Jerseyans turning 65](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/medicare-turning-65/): The parts, the deadlines, the 2026 costs and the penalties that last a lifetime. Here is how to get Medicare right the first time, with a month-by-month plan and free help from SHIP.
- [Medicare Advantage or Medigap? How to choose in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/advantage-vs-medigap/): Open enrollment runs October 15 to December 7. Here is how the two paths really differ, the New Jersey Medigap rules most people never hear about, and the questions to ask before you sign.
- [NJ FamilyCare and MLTSS: how Medicaid pays for long-term care](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/medicaid-mltss-nj/): Medicare does not pay for long-term care. In New Jersey, Medicaid's MLTSS program can, at home, in assisted living or in a nursing home. Here are the 2026 limits, the five-year look-back and how to apply.
- [Staying well in New Jersey: falls, checkups, hearing and more](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/healthy-aging-nj/): Free balance classes, the Medicare checkups you are already paying for, cheaper hearing aids, and where to turn in a heat wave or a hard month. A practical wellness guide for New Jerseyans 60 and up.
- [When a parent leaves the hospital: a New Jersey family guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/hospital-discharge-nj/): Observation versus inpatient, the 3-day rule for rehab coverage, how to appeal a discharge, and a checklist for the day your parent comes home.

## Caregiving

- [How to talk with a parent about getting help at home](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/first-conversation-about-care/): A practical guide for adult children in New Jersey: the signs it is time, how to open the conversation, what to avoid, and the first calls to make.
- [Help for family caregivers in NJ: respite, leave and support](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/caregiver-respite-nj/): New Jersey helps pay for breaks, adult day care and paid leave for people caring for an older relative. Here is who qualifies, what it covers and how to apply.
- [When to call a geriatric care manager, and what they actually do](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/geriatric-care-manager-nj/): A care manager is a professional guide for families facing aging, illness or a sudden crisis. Here is what they do, what to ask, and how to find a good one in New Jersey.
- [How to choose a home care agency in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/home-care-agency-nj/): What New Jersey law requires of home care companies, how to check a license in minutes, what care costs and who pays, and the questions that separate a good agency from a risky one.
- [After a dementia diagnosis: where New Jersey families can turn](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/dementia-support-nj/): Helplines, memory cafes, adult day and respite programs, safety steps and the legal planning to do now, for New Jersey families facing Alzheimer's or another dementia.

## Housing & Legal

- [Aging in place in NJ: making your home safe and comfortable](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/aging-in-place-nj/): Room by room changes, what they cost, who can help pay and how to hire a contractor safely in New Jersey, from split-levels to shore condos.
- [Estate planning basics for New Jersey seniors](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/estate-planning-nj/): Wills, powers of attorney, advance directives, POLST, inheritance tax and probate, explained in plain English for New Jersey families.
- [Where to live next: senior housing choices in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/housing-options-nj/): From staying put to a continuing care community, here is what each option offers, what care costs in New Jersey, and what to ask before you sign.
- [Selling the family home in New Jersey: a downsizing guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/downsizing-nj/): A realistic timeline, how to sort a lifetime of belongings, and the New Jersey tax rules every older seller should know before listing.

## Things to Do

- [Free and discounted things to do in New Jersey after 60](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/free-and-discounted-nj/): Park passes, half-price train rides, tuition-free college classes and free museums. Here is what New Jersey residents 60 and older can get for little or nothing, and how to claim it.
- [20 easy day trips in New Jersey, region by region](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/day-trips-nj/): Lighthouses, gardens, museums and wildlife drives, with honest notes on stairs, walking distances and the best season to go.
- [15 New Jersey museums and historic sites worth the drive](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/nj-museums-guide/): From Edison's lab in West Orange to a battleship on the Delaware, here is what to see at each stop, how easy it is to get around, and what seniors pay.
- [New Jersey gardens and easy walks, with the benches and restrooms noted](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/gardens-and-easy-walks-nj/): Arboretums, iris beds, cherry trees and flat paths along the canal and the bay. Here is what the ground is like at each one, where to sit, and when to go.
- [The Jersey Shore after Labor Day: a town-by-town guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/nj-shore-off-season/): Quiet beaches, easy parking and boardwalks you can actually stroll. Here is what stays open, where beach wheelchairs and mats are, and how to get there without driving.
- [15 places in New Jersey to take the grandkids](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/grandkids-day-out-nj/): Zoos, aquariums, farms and a battleship, chosen for children and grandparents alike. Here is where the benches, elevators and wheelchair rentals are, and what seniors pay.

## Living Well

- [Learn something new after 60: classes and lessons across New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/learn-something-new/): From Osher courses at Rutgers to piano lessons in your own living room, here is where older New Jerseyans can keep learning, and why stretching your brain is worth it.
- [Staying connected: how to beat loneliness in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/staying-connected-nj/): Loneliness is a health risk, and the U.S. Surgeon General has said so plainly. Here are the senior centers, volunteer roles, phone and visitor programs, and tech help that can bring more people into your week.
- [Scams targeting New Jersey seniors now, and how to shut them down](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/scams-nj/): Fake grandkids, fake toll bills, fake PSE&G shutoffs. Learn the scripts scammers use, the red flags that give them away, and exactly who to call in New Jersey if money is already gone.
- [Driving later in life in New Jersey: safety, rules and options](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/driving-later-nj/): New Jersey's license rules, refresher courses that can trim points, the warning signs to watch for, and how to get around when it is time to drive less.
- [Pickleball after 60 in New Jersey: how to get started](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/pickleball-nj/): The paddle sport filling New Jersey's park courts is easy to learn, cheap to try and very social. Here is how to find a game, what to buy and how to avoid the common injuries.
- [How to stay active and social through a New Jersey winter](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/winter-in-nj/): Indoor walking spots, the gym benefit hiding in your Medicare plan, warming centers and the real risks of shoveling. A practical plan for the cold months.
- [Home Happenings: lessons and activities that come to your living room](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/home-happenings/): A New Jersey company that sends checked local pros to older adults' homes to teach music, art, yoga, cooking, games, tech and more, starting in Essex and Passaic counties.
